page: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Dldsv6 family. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores running at 4.2 GHz, utilizing hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 236 GB, and the instance is capable of premium storage.

In benchmark testing, the D4lds_v6 demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2141.0 and single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 31.32 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show relative limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 3990.56 and the Passmark memory score of 1693.71 fall into the lower performance tier. Memory bandwidth tests also indicate weaker read performance, with large block read-only bandwidth measured at 36.76 GB/sec. Conversely, write bandwidth for large blocks remains in the average tier at 25.84 GB/sec.

The low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2 positions this instance as a compute-focused option where memory capacity is not the primary requirement. This resource profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles and fast single-core execution without the overhead of larger memory allocations. Supported by advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX, it is suitable for lightweight vector calculations, single-threaded text processing, and basic web serving. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale software compilation, or highly parallelized multi-threaded tasks due to its memory bandwidth and multi-core constraints.
